claim: The 2021-24 widening of the within-country income gap in formal saving is genuine (scale-free) disequalization
test: pop-weighted mean d(log-odds gap) = d[logit(rich60)-logit(poor40)] 2021->2024 + level jackknife + sign share; secondary weighted corr d(saving overall)~d(log-odds gap) + terciles
effect: PRIMARY mean dL=+0.109 (odds ratio x1.115), below +0.20 threshold; level jackknife FLIPS to -0.115 (drop-top-5); only 47.3% of economies widened (n=55). SECONDARY r=+0.176 (n=55), below 0.30. Exploratory context: dev aggregate ratio poorest40 x1.589 vs richest60 x1.516 (poorest grew proportionally FASTER); dL terciles low/mid/high = -0.050/+0.130/+0.140
gates: G3 ok (headline fin17a_17a1_d all series), G4 ok (70c, 96.2% pop on income-slice frame), G5 n/a, G6 FAIL on secondary (+0.176 -> -0.149, sign flip, retention -0.85); primary level-jackknife sign-unstable
note: PEEK-DISCLOSED (amendment #1): E20's logged aggregate levels made the AGGREGATE ratio derivable by arithmetic, so that comparison is exploratory context and any keep would have been keep-exploratory -- moot, all three pre-registered conditions fail. Closes out the candidate E20 explicitly left open: the +6.1pp pp-scale widening (14.4->20.5) is LARGELY LOW-BASE ARITHMETIC, not scale-free disequalization -- on the log-odds scale the pop-weighted gap barely moved, under half of economies widened, and dropping the 5 largest economies flips the sign to narrowing.
